directive:
ORCHESTRATOR DIRECTIVE (open-obligation resolution for thm:beta-invariance, thm:oracle-high-s, oeq:deficient-frontier). This is a DIRECTION with real content, produced from a source-verified literature extraction plus two adversarial math consultations. Do NOT blind re-solve; follow the construction. Both headline statements CHANGE — the unrestricted claims are not reachable under the frozen assumptions, and the restricted ones below ARE. Adjusting the target this way is required; strengthening an assumption to save the unrestricted claim is FORBIDDEN.

=========================================================
PART 0 — WHY THE PREVIOUS ATTEMPTS FAILED, AND WHAT FIXES IT
=========================================================
Diagnosis, verified against Bonvini-Kennedy arXiv:2207.11825v2 (Appendix, proof of Thm 3.1, Step 1). Their h^{alpha wedge beta} comes from exactly two objects:
    Delta_4(x) = int K_ht(a) pi(a|x) da - pi(t|x)                          ||Delta_4||_inf <~ h^beta
    Delta_5(x) = 1/pi(t|x) - 1/int K_ht(a) pi(a|x) da = Delta_4/[pi(t|x)(pi(t|x)+Delta_4)]   <~ h^beta
Delta_4 is "the h-smoothed treatment density minus its point value at t". Delta_5 exists ONLY because the estimator normalizes by the POINT VALUE 1/pi(t|x) rather than by the localized average int K_ht pi. That is precisely the Nadaraya-Watson local-constant normalization defect. It is an estimator artifact, not a property of the class.
The removal mechanism is LOCAL-POLYNOMIAL DESIGN ADAPTIVITY, and the key point is that it needs POSITIVITY ONLY, no smoothness of any design density: Fan (1992) JASA Table 1 (NW bias carries m' f'/f, local-linear bias does not); Ruppert-Wand (1994) Ann. Statist. Thm 4.1 (odd degree => leading bias free of f); Audibert-Tsybakov (2007) Ann. Statist. 35(2) Thm 3.2, Remark 3.1 and proof eq. (6.2), which lower-bounds the local-polynomial Gram from mu_min alone with NO continuity or differentiability of the design density; KBRW (2024) Ann. Statist. 52(2) Prop. 1 and Prop. A.1 (polynomial reproduction with an arbitrary positive weight absorbed into the Gram; eigenvalues bounded below from positivity). Kennedy-Ma-McHugh-Small (2017) JRSSB Thm 3 already exhibits a dose-response bias b_h(a) = theta''(a)(h^2/2) int u^2 K with the treatment design density appearing ONLY in the variance, and discharges it by citing Fan (1993) Thm 1.
The critical design decision: localize on the MARGINAL treatment density, not conditionally on x. Positivity gives c <= f_A(a) = int pi(a|x) p_X(x) dx <= 1/c with NO smoothness, so the local-polynomial Gram is MARGINAL, EMPIRICAL and controlled by positivity alone. A conditional-in-x Gram D(x) = int s_h s_h^T K_ht pi(a|x) da is NOT empirically estimable (one observation per x) and must NOT be used — using pihat in it degrades the exact reproduction identity and reintroduces the error. This is what the previous window-regressogram and direct-kernel attempts got wrong: they exposed treatment-density bias instead of removing it.

=========================================================
PART 1 — THE ESTIMATOR (construct it as a definition, replacing the prose handle)
=========================================================
Replace def:beta-free-handle (currently a prose handle, which is why it supported no proof) by this fully specified estimator.
Fix a bounded nonnegative kernel K supported on [-1,1] and bounded below on a neighbourhood of 0. Set p = floor(alpha), S(u) = (1,u,...,u^p)^T, K_h(a) = h^{-1} K((a-t_0)/h), S_h(a) = S((a-t_0)/h).
Split the sample into four folds I_mu, I_X, I_lp, I_aux, each of order n (I_aux is reserved and unused by the first-order estimator).
SLICE PILOTS. Partition [0,1]^d into cubes B_1,...,B_J of diameter <= C_d delta. On I_mu with pilot treatment window b, let
    N_j = #{i in I_mu : X_i in B_j},   N_{j,b} = #{i in I_mu : X_i in B_j, |A_i - t_0| <= b}
    muhat_0(x) = (sum_{i in I_mu} Y_i 1{X_i in B_j, |A_i - t_0| <= b}) / N_{j,b}  for x in B_j when N_{j,b} > 0, and 0 when N_{j,b} = 0
    pihat_0(x) = clip_{[c/2, 2/c]} { N_{j,b} / (2 b (N_j vee 1)) }  for x in B_j
Extend both CONSTANTLY in the dose coordinate: muhat(a,x) = muhat_0(x), pihat(a|x) = pihat_0(x). This uses only smoothness the class actually has (x-smoothness holds at the slice t_0 ONLY, so no off-slice x-regularity may be used anywhere).
EMPIRICAL MARGINALIZATIONS on the independent fold I_X:
    mhat(a) = |I_X|^{-1} sum_{l in I_X} muhat(a, X_l),    fhat(a) = |I_X|^{-1} sum_{l in I_X} pihat(a | X_l)
PSEUDO-OUTCOME for i in I_lp:
    xihat_i = { fhat(A_i) / pihat(A_i | X_i) } { Y_i - muhat(A_i, X_i) } + mhat(A_i)
EMPIRICAL MARGINAL GRAM AND SCORE on I_lp (N_lp = |I_lp|):
    Dhat_h = N_lp^{-1} sum_{i in I_lp} K_h(A_i) S_h(A_i) S_h(A_i)^T
    Rhat_h = N_lp^{-1} sum_{i in I_lp} K_h(A_i) S_h(A_i) xihat_i
ESTIMATOR, with lambda_* a fixed constant strictly below the population lower eigenvalue supplied by positivity:
    thetahat_{h,b,delta} = clip_{[-M_Y, M_Y]} [ e_0^T Dhat_h^{-1} Rhat_h * 1{ lambda_min(Dhat_h) >= lambda_* } ]
Everything is Borel measurable, including the value 0 on the bad-Gram event, so the estimator lies in the frozen def:estimator-class.

=========================================================
PART 2 — THE LEMMA CHAIN TO PROVE (each is a separate node; prove, do not posit)
=========================================================
(L-a) ORACLE PSEUDO-OUTCOME IDENTITY. With f_A(a) = int pi(a|x) p_X(x) dx and theta(a) = int mu(a,x) p_X(x) dx, the oracle pseudo-outcome xi_P = {f_A(A)/pi(A|X)}{Y - mu(A,X)} + theta(A) satisfies E_P(xi_P | A = a) = theta(a), because the residual has conditional mean zero given (A,X). Hence local-polynomial regression of xi_P on the MARGINAL A localizes the scalar partial-mean curve a -> theta(a), whose intercept at t_0 is the target theta_P(t_0).
(L-b) MARGINAL POSITIVITY WITHOUT SMOOTHNESS. c <= f_A(a) <= 1/c for all a, directly from the frozen two-sided positivity, with NO smoothness and NO lower bound on p_X (p_X integrates to one; the lower bound on pi alone suffices).
(L-c) HOELDER TRANSFER TO THE PARTIAL MEAN. a -> theta(a) is Hoelder-alpha with radius L, inherited by integrating the uniform-in-x Hoelder-alpha property of a -> mu(a,x) against p_X. Handle the measurability/domination explicitly; |Y| <= M_Y supplies domination.
(L-d) DESIGN-ADAPTIVE ORACLE BIAS. Let D_h = E{K_h(A) S_h(A) S_h(A)^T}, W_h(a) = e_0^T D_h^{-1} S_h(a) K_h(a), and vartheta_h = e_0^T D_h^{-1} E{K_h(A) S_h(A) xi_P(Z)}. Then W_h reproduces polynomials of degree <= p against f_A, i.e. int W_h(a) q(a) f_A(a) da = q(t_0) for every such q, and therefore
        | vartheta_h - theta(t_0) | <= C h^alpha.
    NO derivative and NO Hoelder modulus of f_A appears. This is the whole point: it is where the beta dies. Cite Audibert-Tsybakov (2007) Thm 3.2 / eq. (6.2) and KBRW Prop. 1 / Prop. A.1 for the mechanism; the reproduction itself is algebraic given the Gram.
(L-e) EXACT DOUBLE-ROBUST REMAINDER IDENTITY. For arbitrary clipped pilots mutilde, pitilde write v_a(x) = mutilde(a,x) - mu(a,x), e_a(x) = pitilde(a|x) - pi(a|x), ebar_a = P_X e_a, f_a = P_X pi(a|.), mtilde(a) = P_X mutilde(a,.), ftilde(a) = P_X pitilde(a|.). Then Bayes' rule gives E(xitilde | A = a) = theta(a) + B(a) with the EXACT remainder
        B(a) = P_X[ v_a e_a / pitilde_a ] - (ebar_a / f_a) P_X[ v_a pi_a / pitilde_a ]
    hence |B(a)| <= C(c) ||v_a||_{L_2(P_X)} ||e_a||_{L_2(P_X)}. NO term carries e_a alone — every treatment-density error is multiplied by a regression discrepancy.
(L-f) OFF-SLICE CONTROL. Write A = alpha wedge 1, B = beta wedge 1, U = ||mutilde(t_0,.) - mu(t_0,.)||_2, V = ||pitilde(t_0|.) - pi(t_0|.)||_2. With the constant-in-a extension, for |a - t_0| <= h,
        ||v_a||_2 <= U + L h^A,     ||e_a||_2 <= V + L h^B
    and therefore sup_{|a-t_0|<=h} |B(a)| <= C[ UV + U h^B + V h^A + h^{A+B} ].
    BE HONEST ABOUT THIS: h^{A+B} is a STRUCTURAL residual that survives even at U = V = 0, because the off-slice product {mu(a,x)-mu(t_0,x)}{pi(a|x)-pi(t_0|x)} may depend on x arbitrarily and the class assumes NO x-smoothness off the slice. It is NOT removable by better pilots. This is exactly why the theorems below are regime-restricted.
(L-g) PILOT MSE BOUNDS. E U^2 <~ delta^{2(s wedge 1)} + b^{2A} + (n b delta^d)^{-1} and E V^2 <~ delta^{2(s wedge 1)} + b^{2B} + (n b delta^d)^{-1}, by the same binomial argument as the frozen lem:explicit-histogram-window-upper; empty-cell contributions absorb into the last term.
(L-h) GOOD-GRAM PROBABILITY. Since p is fixed and f_A >= c, matrix concentration gives P{ lambda_min(Dhat_h) < lambda_* } <= C exp(-c_1 n h).
(L-i) CONDITIONAL VARIANCE. On the good-Gram event and conditional on the training folds, Var(thetahat) <= C/(nh) + C/n, the n^{-1} term covering the empirical marginalization over I_X.
(L-j) MASTER RISK INEQUALITY. Combining (L-d)-(L-i), with u = delta^{s wedge 1} + b^A + (n b delta^d)^{-1/2} and v = delta^{s wedge 1} + b^B + (n b delta^d)^{-1/2}, for EVERY admissible (h,b,delta):
        E( thetahat_{h,b,delta} - theta(t_0) )^2 <= C[ h^{2 alpha} + { (u + h^A)(v + h^B) }^2 + 1/(nh) + 1/n + exp(-c_1 n h) ].
    This is an explicit inequality valid at every tuning, in the same style as the frozen regressogram lemma, and it is a genuine strict advance on it: the treatment bias is a true design-adaptive h^alpha with no marginal-density smoothness.

=========================================================
PART 3 — THE REGIONS, THE TUNING, AND THE THRESHOLD (do the algebra, do not guess)
=========================================================
Notation: A = alpha wedge 1, B = beta wedge 1, k = 1/(2 alpha + 1), tau_alpha = alpha/(2 alpha + 1).
STRUCTURAL REGION:
    R = { (alpha,beta) : A + B >= alpha } = { alpha <= 1 } union { 1 < alpha <= 2 and beta >= alpha - 1 }.
    NOTE CAREFULLY: R contains NO point with alpha > 2, however large beta is. Do not claim beta >= alpha - 1 suffices when alpha > 2.
On R, h^{A+B} <= h^alpha, so expanding (u+h^A)(v+h^B) = uv + u h^B + v h^A + h^{A+B}, the purely deterministic treatment contribution is O(h^{2 alpha}) and every REMAINING beta-dependent term contains a statistical pilot error. (The cross terms are u h^B and v h^A; beta also enters v, hence uv.)
TUNING. Take h ~ n^{-k}, so h^{2 alpha} ~ 1/(nh) ~ n^{-2 alpha/(2 alpha+1)}. Allocate pilot rates u = O(n^{-k z}), v = O(n^{-k(alpha - z)}); then uv = O(h^alpha) automatically, u h^B = O(h^alpha) iff z >= alpha - B, and v h^A = O(h^alpha) iff z <= A. So the feasible interval is
    I = [ (alpha - B)_+ , A ],   nonempty EXACTLY on R.
For z in I put m(z) = max{z, alpha - z}, rho(z) = max{ z/A, (alpha - z)/B }, and choose
    b ~ n^{-k rho(z)},    delta ~ n^{-k m(z)/(s wedge 1)},
which give b^A <~ n^{-kz}, b^B <~ n^{-k(alpha-z)}, delta^{s wedge 1} = n^{-k m(z)}. The stochastic pilot term (n b delta^d)^{-1/2} <~ n^{-k m(z)} holds iff
    (s wedge 1) >= G(z) := d m(z) / { 2 alpha + 1 - rho(z) - 2 m(z) }.
THRESHOLD: g(alpha,beta,d) := min_{z in I} G(z), attained at
    z_* = alpha/2                              if B >= A;
    z_* = max{ alpha/2, alpha - B }            if B < A and B >= tau_alpha;
    z_* = alpha A / (A + B)                    if B < A and B < tau_alpha.
Closed form (verify each branch yourself; they agree at the boundaries and all denominators are positive on R):
    g = d alpha / (2 alpha + 2 - alpha/A)                 if B >= A;
    g = d alpha / (2 alpha + 2 - alpha/B)                 if B < A, B >= tau_alpha, B >= alpha/2;
    g = d (alpha - B) / (2 B)                             if B < A, B >= tau_alpha, B < alpha/2;
    g = d alpha A / { A - alpha + (2 alpha + 1) B }       if B < A, B < tau_alpha.
ORACLE REGION:
    Omega = { (alpha,beta,s,d) : A + B >= alpha  and  (s wedge 1) >= g(alpha,beta,d) }.
    Because the pilot bound carries s wedge 1, the condition genuinely requires BOTH g <= 1 and s >= g; if g > 1 this proof gets no help from larger s. Omega is nonempty: e.g. alpha = 1/2, B >= 1/2, d = 1 gives g = 1/4 so s >= 1/4 suffices; alpha = beta = 1 gives g = d/3.
    DO NOT write s >= d/4. That threshold is NOT what this construction gives, and inserting it would be assuming the crux. Bonvini-Kennedy's own s >= d/4 is proved only under the extra hypothesis alpha <= beta, which is exactly the hypothesis this run removes; deleting their hypothesis while keeping their threshold is forbidden.

=========================================================
PART 4 — THE REPLACEMENT STATEMENTS
=========================================================
thm:oracle-high-s — RESTATE as the restricted oracle-rate theorem:
    For every fixed parameter tuple in Omega there exist n-free constants 0 < C_low <= C_up < infinity with
        C_low n^{-2 alpha/(2 alpha+1)} <= M_n <= C_up n^{-2 alpha/(2 alpha+1)}   for all sufficiently large n.
    Lower half = the frozen lem:all-beta-oracle-lower-floor. Upper half = (L-j) at h ~ n^{-1/(2 alpha+1)}, b ~ n^{-rho(z_*)/(2 alpha+1)}, delta ~ n^{-m(z_*)/{(2 alpha+1)(s wedge 1)}}, using uv, u h^B, v h^A, h^{A+B} all O(h^alpha), 1/(nh) ~ h^{2 alpha}, and n^{-1}, exp(-c_1 n h) negligible. Rename the node id only if your schema requires it; the s >= d/4 hypothesis is DELETED and replaced by membership in Omega.
thm:beta-invariance — RESTATE as restricted beta-invariance:
    Fix 0 < beta < beta' < infinity and suppose the ROUGH exponent beta satisfies (alpha,beta,s,d) in Omega. Then
        C_low n^{-2 alpha/(2 alpha+1)} <= M_n(beta') <= M_n(beta) <= C_up(beta) n^{-2 alpha/(2 alpha+1)},
    hence M_n(beta) and M_n(beta') agree up to n-free constants, with 1 <= M_n(beta)/M_n(beta') <= C_up(beta)/C_low.
    Proof skeleton, and MIND THE DIRECTION: (1) the upper bound is proved on the ROUGH class (exponent beta) — this is the whole point, since rough is the larger class; (2) the frozen all-beta lower floor applies to the SMOOTHER class (beta'); (3) frozen lem:beta-class-one-sided-monotonicity gives M_n(beta) >= M_n(beta'); (4) monotonicity also transfers the rough-class upper bound to every nested smoother class, so no separate threshold condition on beta' is needed.
    This is CONSTANT-FACTOR equivalence, not ratio convergence to 1. Constants may depend on beta and the other fixed parameters but not on n; do NOT advertise uniformity over a continuum of beta unless you separately establish uniform constants — state the pairwise-fixed-(beta,beta') form.
oeq:deficient-frontier — RESTATE to cover exactly the two regions this proof leaves open, and nothing more:
    (i) the structural complement A + B < alpha, equivalently alpha > 1 + min(beta,1) (for beta < 1 this is alpha > 1 + beta; for beta >= 1 it is alpha > 2), where the structural h^{A+B} exceeds h^alpha and the construction does not reach the floor;
    (ii) the region A + B >= alpha but (s wedge 1) < g(alpha,beta,d).
    In BOTH, only the frozen bracket is known. State them as OPEN QUESTIONS. Neither is a lower-bound theorem, so do NOT assert beta-sensitivity there — the honest statement is that the minimax rate is undetermined in those regions.

=========================================================
PART 5 — FORBIDDEN STEPS (each would assume the crux; all were flagged explicitly)
=========================================================
Do not assert that an empirical CONDITIONAL Gram reproduces treatment polynomials pointwise in x; do not replace an empirical conditional Gram by its population version; do not claim h^beta terms multiply only STATISTICAL nuisance error while ignoring the structural off-slice error; do not posit a HOIF remainder such as k^{-2s/d} without deriving its projection identity; do not apply KBRW's eigenvalue lemma without verifying its design assumptions for the present p_X; do not use smoothness of x -> d_a^j mu(t_0,x) or x -> d_a^j pi(t_0|x) (the class does not assume it); do not add a lower bound or smoothness on p_X; do not import Bonvini-Kennedy's oracle conclusion after deleting their alpha <= beta condition. Add NO new assumption to the class.

=========================================================
DEFECT 1 (a real proof gap) — the E[U^2 V^2] step is not proved
=========================================================
lem:beta-free-master-risk and lem:localized-polynomial-master-risk both use
    E[U^2 V^2] <= C u^2 v^2
and justify it by gesturing at fourth moments. That does not follow from lem:slice-histogram-pilot-mse, which is a SECOND-moment statement. To get it from moments you would have to control E U^4 and E V^4 for the integrated L_2(P_X) norms, including the CROSS-CELL terms in U^4 and V^4 — summing cellwise fourth moments is not enough. Both headline theorems currently inherit this gap. Do not paper over it.

=========================================================
DEFECT 2 (non-maximality) — your two pilots needlessly share one fold, one b and one delta
=========================================================
Your own def:beta-free-handle splits the sample into FOUR folds I_mu, I_X, I_lp, I_aux and then leaves I_aux entirely unused, while estimating BOTH pilots on I_mu with a single (b, delta). That is wasteful in two separate ways: it makes U and V dependent (which is what forces the unproved fourth-moment step), and it forces a single tuning pair to serve two pilots with different exponents (A for the regression pilot, B for the density pilot), which inflates the threshold.

=========================================================
THE FIX — SEPARATE, INDEPENDENT PILOTS ON DISJOINT FOLDS
=========================================================
Estimate the two pilots on DISJOINT folds with their OWN tuning parameters:
  - mu(t_0, .) on I_mu with (b_mu, delta_mu);
  - pi(t_0 | .) INDEPENDENTLY on I_aux with (b_pi, delta_pi).
Everything else in def:beta-free-handle stays as you wrote it (constant-in-a extension, positivity clipping, empirical marginalizations on I_X, degree-floor(alpha) local polynomial on I_lp, empirical marginal Gram, clipping to [-M_Y,M_Y], zeroing on the bad-Gram event, measurability).

This fix closes DEFECT 1 OUTRIGHT: U and V are now functions of independent folds, so
    E[U^2 V^2] = E[U^2] E[V^2] <= C u^2 v^2
by independence alone. Delete the fourth-moment argument entirely and replace it with this one-line independence step. Do NOT keep a fourth-moment claim as a fallback.

It also STRICTLY IMPROVES the threshold. With S = s wedge 1,
    u = delta_mu^S + b_mu^A + (n b_mu delta_mu^d)^{-1/2},
    v = delta_pi^S + b_pi^B + (n b_pi delta_pi^d)^{-1/2}.
For z in I = [(alpha - B)_+ , A], choose
    b_mu ~ n^{-k z / A},      delta_mu ~ n^{-k z / S},
    b_pi ~ n^{-k (alpha - z) / B},   delta_pi ~ n^{-k (alpha - z) / S},   with k = 1/(2 alpha + 1).
Then the exact new threshold is
    g_sep(alpha, beta, d) = min_{z in I} max{ d z / (2 alpha + 1 - z/A - 2 z),  d (alpha - z) / (2 alpha + 1 - (alpha - z)/B - 2 (alpha - z)) },
the minimization being restricted to z with BOTH denominators positive. Derive its CLOSED FORM the same way you derived g (identify where the two branches of the max cross, and the monotonicity of each branch in z), state the branch conditions explicitly, and verify the branches agree at their boundaries.
Prove g_sep <= g, and record that the inequality is sometimes STRICT — worked check you should reproduce: at alpha = 0.4 (so A = 0.4), beta = 0.2 (so B = 0.2), d = 1, the shared-pilot threshold is g = 4/9 ~ 0.4444 while g_sep ~ 0.2924. changed.from:
{"id":"def:oracle-threshold","name":"g","construction":"Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).","free_symbols":["g","alpha","beta","d"],"inputs":["alpha","beta","d"]}

=========================================================================
Finding (math referee): "Given the stated compatible bridge mu_P = m_P a.e. ... the proof identifies
theta_P(t_0) without using consistency or exchangeability; remove them from this proposition OR DERIVE THE
BRIDGE FROM THEM." Take the DERIVE branch. Deleting consistency and exchangeability while retaining the
assumed bridge is REJECTED and must not be re-proposed: it preserves the assume-your-own-conclusion defect
the finding is about.

Root cause: the current statement HYPOTHESISES mu_P = m_P a.e. and then integrates, which is why its own
proof says "neither consistency nor conditional exchangeability was used". Additionally, the current
POINTWISE condition Y(a) indep A | X for every fixed a is too weak to ever derive the bridge: for
A ~ Unif[0,1], Y = 1, Y(a) = 1{A=a}, every fixed coordinate is 0 a.s., so under the coordinate sigma-field
the family is independent of A while a -> E[Y|A=a] = 1; the bridge fails everywhere. So the pointwise form

    \(\theta_P(t_0)=\int\mu_P(t_0,x)p_X(x)\,dx=\mathbb E[Y(t_0)]\). RETAIN the obstruction half: consistency
    and process-level exchangeability alone do not identify the causal mean at the null event \(A=t_0\).

14. PROOF, paired in `proofs` (`argues_proposed: true`), following this route:
    (i)   standard Borel \(\mathsf Y\) and covariate space give a regular conditional law
          \(K_x=\mathcal L(\mathbf Y\mid X=x)\);
    (ii)  set \(m_P(a,x)=\int_{\mathsf Y}e(y,a)\,K_x(dy)\); bounded joint measurability of \(e\) plus
          kernel measurability make it jointly Borel, and for each fixed \(a\) it is a version of
          \(\mathbb E[Y(a)\mid X=x]\);
    (iii) process exchangeability gives \(\mathcal L(\mathbf Y\mid A,X)=K_X\) a.s., hence
          \(\mathbb E[e(\mathbf Y,A)\mid A,X]=\int e(y,A)K_X(dy)=m_P(A,X)\);
    (iv)  consistency gives \(Y=e(\mathbf Y,A)\) a.s., so \(\mathbb E[Y\mid A,X]=m_P(A,X)\);
    (v)   \(\mu_P(A,X)\) is also a version of \(\mathbb E[Y\mid A,X]\), so \(\mu_P=m_P\) for

directive:
CORRECTION ROUND. The previous round's wholesale repair was ACCEPTED and 19 of its 20 variants are applied:
the pbar deletion, the pbar-free headline functional, the standard-Borel path typing, process-level
exchangeability, the derived-bridge proposition and the disclosure prose are all in the proto. Do NOT
re-open any of that. Four narrow defects remain. Fix exactly these and nothing else.

DEFECT 1 (SOUNDNESS — the important one). ass:potential-outcome-path-typing currently reads
"... such that \(Y(a)=e(\mathbf Y,a)\) almost surely for every \(a\in[0,1]\)". That is a per-dose null set,
one for each of uncountably many \(a\). The proposition's proof then takes the step
"\(Y(A)=e(\mathbf Y,A)\) almost surely" AT THE RANDOM DOSE \(A\), and that does NOT follow: the union of
uncountably many null sets need not be null. This is precisely the diagonal pathology the whole path-space
repair exists to eliminate — it is the same defect, one level down, and it would make the derived bridge
unsound.

Emit `assumption-replace` on ass:potential-outcome-path-typing whose condition makes the evaluation
identity hold IDENTICALLY, not almost surely. Keep everything else about the node. The condition must read
(adjust only for house style):
  There exist a standard Borel space \((\mathsf Y,\mathcal Y)\), a
  \(\mathcal Y\otimes\mathcal B([0,1])/\mathcal B([-M_Y,M_Y])\)-measurable evaluation map
  \(e:\mathsf Y\times[0,1]\to[-M_Y,M_Y]\), and an \(\mathcal F/\mathcal Y\)-measurable random element
  \(\mathbf Y\) on the underlying probability space such that \(Y(a)=e(\mathbf Y,a)\) holds for every
  \(a\in[0,1]\) and at every sample point; that is, the potential-outcome family IS the evaluation of
  \(\mathbf Y\).
Keep the `not_crux` content: it remains a measurability/typing condition on the causal completion that
constrains no observed-data law, is not a member property of the Hoelder class, and is consumed by no
statistical rate result. Note in the reason WHY the strengthening from "almost surely for every a" to an
identity is needed: it is exactly what licenses evaluation at the random dose.

Then RE-EMIT the proof of prop:causal-identification-at-t0 against the corrected assumption. The proof is
otherwise correct and should be preserved essentially verbatim — including the canonical kernel version
\(\overline m_P\), the Tonelli reconciliation of the proposition's \(m_P\) with \(\overline m_P\), the
positivity upgrade, the transport to \(t_0\), and the two-point standard-Borel obstruction witness. The ONLY
change is that the step \(Y(A)=e(\mathbf Y,A)\) is now IMMEDIATE from the typing identity rather than an
almost-sure claim; say so explicitly instead of asserting it "almost surely". Do not change the
proposition's STATEMENT — it is correct as applied.

`standard: {name: "process-level conditional exchangeability", cite: "KennedyMaMcHughSmall2017"}`.

VERBATIM STATEMENT (restore exactly):
Fix \(0<c<1\), and put \(B_*=\alpha\vee\beta\) and
\[
r_{\mathrm f}(\alpha,\beta,s,d)
=
\frac{8}{4+2/B_*+d/s}.
\]
For every admissible finite \(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,t_0\), there are constants \(C_{\mathrm f}>0\) and \(n_0\in\mathbb N\), independent of \(n\), such that, for every \(n\ge n_0\),
\[
\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)
\ge C_{\mathrm f}n^{-r_{\mathrm f}(\alpha,\beta,s,d)}.
\]
Together with Lemma~\texttt{lem:all-beta-oracle-lower-floor}, this gives
\[
\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)
\ge
C n^{-\min\{2\alpha/(2\alpha+1),r_{\mathrm f}(\alpha,\beta,s,d)\}}.
\]
The new fuzzy lower bound is strictly stronger than the oracle floor exactly when
\[
\frac ds>4+\frac4\alpha-\frac{2}{\alpha\vee\beta}.
\]

I verified the arithmetic myself in exact rational arithmetic. With R=1, V=k and t=k/4 that node yields exponent
  t^2 / (2(V + R t/3)) = (k^2/16) / (2(k + k/12)) = (k^2/16) / (13k/6) = 3k/104,

{"id":"lem:localized-pseudo-outcome-variance","kind":"lemma","statement":"On the good-Gram event, conditional on the pilot folds, the local-polynomial coefficient based on population marginalizations of the pilots has mean-square stochastic error at most \(C/(nh)\) around its population coefficient. \[
G_h=\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\},
\qquad N=|I_{\mathrm{lp}}|,
\]
and condition on \(I_\mu,I_{\mathrm{aux}}\). Put \(\bar f=P_X\widehat\pi_0\), \(\bar m=P_X\widehat\mu_0\), and
\[
\bar\xi_i=
\frac{\bar f}{\widehat\pi_0(X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu_0(X_i)\}+\bar m.
\]
The clipping in Definition~\texttt{def:beta-free-handle} makes \(\bar\xi_i\) uniformly bounded. Define
\[
D_h=\mathbb E_P[K_h(A)S_h(A)S_h(A)^\top],
\qquad
\gamma_h=D_h^{-1}\mathbb E_P[K_h(A)S_h(A)\bar\xi].
\]
The preceding design lemma gives \(\|D_h^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\|\gamma_h\|\le C\). Exact normal-equation algebra yields, on \(G_h\),
\[
\widehat\gamma_h-\gamma_h
=
\widehat D_h^{-1}\frac1N\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}
K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\{\bar\xi_i-S_h(A_i)^\top\gamma_h\}.
\]
The summands are conditionally iid and centered, with second moments bounded by \(C/h\); also \(\|\widehat D_h^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le1/\lambda_*\) on \(G_h\). Therefore
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\mathbf1_{G_h}\lvert e_0^\top(\widehat\gamma_h-\gamma_h)\rvert^2
\,\middle|\,I_\mu,I_{\mathrm{aux}}\right]
\le\frac{C}{Nh}\le\frac{C}{nh}.
\]
For empirical marginalizations, set
\[
\Delta_m=P_{I_X}\widehat\mu_0-P_X\widehat\mu_0,
\quad
\Delta_f=P_{I_X}\widehat\pi_0-P_X\widehat\pi_0,
\quad
q_i=\frac{Y_i-\widehat\mu_0(X_i)}{\widehat\pi_0(X_i)}.
\]
Conditional independence and boundedness give \(\mathbb E_P(\Delta_m^2+\Delta_f^2\mid I_\mu,I_{\mathrm{aux}})\le C/n\). Since \(S_h(a)^\top e_0=1\),
\[
e_0^\top(\widehat\gamma_h^{\mathrm{emp}}-\widehat\gamma_h^{\mathrm{pop}})
=
\Delta_m+\Delta_fT_h,
\qquad
T_h=e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}P_{I_{\mathrm{lp}}}(K_hS_hq).
\]
Let \(J=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}\mathbf1\{K_h(A_i)>0\}\). If \(\lfloor\alpha\rfloor=0\), \(T_h\) is a kernel-weighted average of bounded \(q_i\). Otherwise, invertibility on \(G_h\) implies \(J\ge\lfloor\alpha\rfloor+1\ge2\) and
\[
\mathbf1_{G_h}|T_h|\le C\mathbf1_{\{J\ge2\}}J/(Nh).
\]
When \(Nh\le1\), the binomial factorial moment \(\mathbb E[J(J-1)]\le C(Nh)^2\) bounds the truncated second moment of \(T_h\). When \(Nh>1\), centering about \(D_h^{-1}\mathbb E_P[K_hS_hq]\) and repeating the preceding variance calculation gives the same uniform bound. Independence of \(I_X\) and \(I_{\mathrm{lp}}\) now yields
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\mathbf1_{G_h}\lvert e_0^\top(\widehat\gamma_h^{\mathrm{emp}}-
\widehat\gamma_h^{\mathrm{pop}})\rvert^2\right]
\le C/n.
\]

{"id":"lem:explicit-histogram-window-upper","kind":"lemma","statement":"Put \(\bar\alpha=\alpha\wedge1\), \(\bar\beta=\beta\wedge1\), and \(\bar s=s\wedge1\). There are constants \(C<\infty\) and \(h_0>0\), independent of \(n\), such that for every \(0<h\le h_0\) and \(0<\delta\le1\) satisfying \(nh\delta^d\ge2^{d+3}\), one explicit split-sample regressogram obeys
\[
\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)
\le C\left\{h^{2\bar\alpha}+\delta^{4\bar s}+\delta^{2\bar s}h^{2\bar\beta}+\frac1{nh\delta^d}+\frac1n\right\}.
\]
For \(h\asymp n^{-u}\), \(\delta\asymp n^{-v}\), and \(u+dv<1\), this gives \(\mathcal M_n=O(n^{-R(u,v)})\), where
\[
R(u,v)=\min\{2\bar\alpha u,4\bar s v,2\bar s v+2\bar\beta u,1-u-dv,1\}.
\]","free_symbols":["alpha","beta","s","d","n","M_n","M_Y","L","c","t_0","Pclass","theta_P","A","X","Y","mu_P","pi_P","P_X"],"depends_on":["ass:iid","ass:mu-version","ass:pi-version","ass:px-version","ass:bounded-outcome","ass:positivity-lower","ass:positivity-upper","ass:mu-a-holder","ass:pi-a-holder","ass:mu-x-holder","ass:pi-x-holder","prop:class-nonempty","prop:estimand-version-invariant","def:holder-class","def:estimator-class","def:minimax-mse"],"proof_tex":"Partition \([0,1]^d\) into \(K\le(2/\delta)^d\) half-open cubes \(B_1,\ldots,B_K\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta\), and split the sample into independent folds \(I_1,I_2\) of sizes \(N_1,N_2\asymp n\). On the first fold put
\[
\widehat p_j=N_1^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_1}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_j\}.
\]
On the second fold let \(\widehat m_j\) be the average of the \(Y_i\) satisfying \(X_i\in B_j\) and \(\lvert A_i-t_0\rvert\le h\), with value zero if the selected cell is empty. Define
\[
\widehat\theta_{h,\delta}=\sum_{j=1}^K\widehat p_j\widehat m_j.
\]
Finite sums, indicator functions, counts, and the assigned empty-cell value make this a Borel element of \(\mathfrak T_n\).

Write \(p_j=P_X(B_j)\) and
\[
q_h(x)=P(\lvert A-t_0\rvert\le h\mid X=x)
=\int_{t_0-h}^{t_0+h}\pi_P(a\mid x)\,da.
\]
For \(h\le h_0:=\min\{t_0,1-t_0\}\), uniform positivity gives
\[
2ch\le q_h(x)\le 2h/c.
\]
Let
\[
m_j=\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X\in B_j,\lvert A-t_0\rvert\le h],
\qquad
\bar\mu_j=\mathbb E_P[\mu_P(t_0,X)\mid X\in B_j],
\]
with arbitrary values when \(p_j=0\). By treatment-direction H\"older continuity,
\[
\left|q_h(x)^{-1}\int_{t_0-h}^{t_0+h}
\mu_P(a,x)\pi_P(a\mid x)\,da-\mu_P(t_0,x)
\right|
\le C h^{\bar\alpha}.
\]
The density H\"older condition similarly yields
\[
\frac{q_h(x)}{2h}=\pi_P(t_0\mid x)+r_h(x),
\qquad \lVert r_h\rVert_\infty\le C h^{\bar\beta}.
\]
On every cell, each of \(x\mapsto\mu_P(t_0,x)\) and \(x\mapsto\pi_P(t_0\mid x)\) has oscillation at most \(C\delta^{\bar s}\). The difference between the \(q_h\)-weighted and unweighted cell means of \(\mu_P(t_0,\cdot)\) is a covariance divided by the cell mean of \(q_h\). After dividing numerator and denominator by \(2h\), the covariance with \(\pi_P(t_0\mid\cdot)\) is bounded by the product of the two cell oscillations, while the covariance with \(r_h\) is bounded by the oscillation of \(\mu_P(t_0,\cdot)\) times \(\lVert r_h\rVert_\infty\). The denominator is at least \(c\). Consequently,
\[
\lvert m_j-\bar\mu_j\rvert
\le C\{h^{\bar\alpha}+\delta^{2\bar s}+\delta^{\bar s}h^{\bar\beta}\}.
\]
Since \(\theta_P(t_0)=\sum_jp_j\bar\mu_j\), the squared approximation bias is at most
\[
C\{h^{2\bar\alpha}+\delta^{4\bar s}+\delta^{2\bar s}h^{2\bar\beta}\}.
\]

It remains to bound sampling error. Conditional on the second fold, \(\lvert\widehat m_j\rvert\le M_Y\), so independence of the folds gives
\[
\mathbb E_P\left[
\left\{\sum_j(\widehat p_j-p_j)\widehat m_j\right\}^2
\,\middle|\,I_2\right]
\le \frac{M_Y^2}{N_1}.
\]
Put
\[
Q_j=P(X\in B_j,\lvert A-t_0\rvert\le h)\ge2chp_j.
\]
If \(N_j\sim\operatorname{Bin}(N_2,Q_j)\) is the selected second-fold count, then
\[
\mathbb E_P\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N_j>0\}}{N_j}\right]
\le\frac{2}{N_2Q_j}.
\]
Conditional on the cell counts, the centered nonempty-cell averages have zero cross-products, and hence their weighted sum has variance at most
\[
C\sum_{j:Q_j>0}\frac{p_j^2}{N_2Q_j}
\le\frac{C}{nh}.
\]
For the total population mass of empty selected cells,
\[
W=\sum_jp_j\mathbf1\{N_j=0\},
\]
one has \(0\le W\le1\), and therefore
\[
\mathbb E_P[W^2]
\le\mathbb E_P[W]
\le\sum_jp_j e^{-N_2Q_j}
\le\frac{CK}{nh}
\le\frac{C}{nh\delta^d}.
\]
Here the penultimate inequality uses \(x e^{-a x}\le1/(ae)\), and constants absorb the fixed fold proportions. Combining approximation bias, the two sampling bounds, and Definition~\texttt{def:minimax-mse} proves the displayed risk inequality uniformly over the class. Finally, substituting \(h\asymp n^{-u}\) and \(\delta\asymp n^{-v}\) gives the five displayed polynomial exponents. The condition \(u+dv<1\) makes the cell-count restriction valid for all sufficiently large \(n\), and taking the smallest exponent proves the last assertion.","status":"proved"}

note:
D0.5 MATH-REFEREE REPAIR ROUND, partial apply: 9 of 10 gated items applied, 1 DROPPED. Codex gpt-5.6-sol adjudicated the full bundle on the canonical packet and returned APPLY on the new lemma, APPLY on the constant fix, and APPLY ON ALL NINE DEPENDENCY REMOVAL SETS, but flagged one trap I had missed, and I verified it myself against the live payload before acting: the statement-replace for lem:unit-positivity-oracle-rate silently sets status to-prove on a node that is currently proved and carries a complete corollary proof, while the proofs channel is empty. Applying it verbatim would have DEMOTED a proved lemma to an unproved obligation and contradicted the prose that advertises it. I measured every statement-replace payload status against the live core: exactly that one differs. So I dropped it and applied the other nine. The drop is lossless: its only content was a dependency trim, pure hygiene, and dropping it leaves the node declaring a few more prerequisites than it strictly consumes, which is harmless and orphans nothing; critically its depends_on still names the new helper lem:unit-positivity-minimal-class-oracle-rate, so that helper stays reachable. Not re-requested.

WHAT THE ROUND FIXED. The D0.5 decision/novelty referee PASSED with zero findings and BOTH cited nodes verified, so only two math findings were open. I ordered them fixed at the root plus ONE exhaustive audit of the same two defect classes across the whole core, rather than patching one instance per round.

Finding 1, concentration-constant: the fuzzy lemma displayed a Rademacher tail bound 2exp(-k/32) while the core's only concentration node is the BERNSTEIN lem:bounded-sum-concentration. I verified the arithmetic myself in exact rational arithmetic before directing the fix: at R=1, V=k, t=k/4 that node yields (k^2/16)/(13k/6) = 3k/104, and 1/32 = 0.03125 exceeds 3/104 = 0.028846, so the displayed constant was strictly tighter than the cited node justifies. The solver took the weaken route and the proof now displays 3k/104. Codex confirmed the rate r_f and the strict-improvement condition d/s > 4 + 4/alpha - 2/(alpha v beta) are UNCHANGED, the weakening touching only an exponentially vanishing exception probability.

Finding 2, redundant-assumption: rather than merely deleting an unused hypothesis, the solver proved a genuinely NEW lemma lem:unit-positivity-minimal-class-oracle-rate giving the exact oracle rate over a strictly LARGER class Q_1 that imposes no covariate-direction Holder condition, no treatment-density smoothness and no p_X regularity, and made the frozen-class boundary result a corollary. Codex ruled it sound on all four checks including strictness of the inclusion. That is a real strengthening, not a deletion.

THE DEPENDENCY REMOVALS WERE THE HIGH-RISK ITEM and I treated them as such, because a dependency removal is exactly what cost this run three proved lemmas to the orphan pruner two rounds ago. Before adjudicating I simulated reachability from roots {thm:*, prop:*, oeq:*} under the proposed graph and found NO newly unreachable node; codex recomputed it independently, got 53 reachable nodes both before and after, and confirmed the finding, and separately confirmed that no node still asserts a result whose supporting node it just stopped depending on. Codex also noted lem:takatsu-westling-pointwise-comparator is unreachable from those roots BOTH before and after, i.e. a pre-existing property of a cited comparator node that has survived every render this run, not damage from this bundle.

directive:
D0.5 DECISION-REFEREE REPAIR — POSITIONING ONLY, FIXED WHOLESALE. Change NO mathematics: every theorem, lemma, proof, exponent, constant, region, assumption and dependency stays exactly as proved. Do NOT close oeq:deficient-frontier. Do NOT reintroduce pbar. Do NOT emit unified-diff '+' markers. This round edits related_work, the comparator promise table, and thm:oracle-high-s's post-statement comparison ONLY.

STATUS: the MATH referee now PASSES with zero findings and both cited nodes verified. One decision-referee finding is open, and it is the third positioning finding on thm:oracle-high-s in this run. The first two were repaired one comparator at a time, which is why a third appeared. Fix the CLASS this time, not the instance.

THE FINDING. `related-work-gap` @ thm:oracle-high-s: "the bibliography includes Schindl--Shen--Kennedy's continuous-exposure minimax work with no relevance/comparison sentence, and the theorem's post-statement comparison should explicitly delimit that edge/incremental target and the closest CATE-minimax fuzzy-hypothesis result from this fixed-dose interior minimax theorem."

TASK 1 — CLOSE THE NAMED GAP. SchindlShenKennedy2024Incremental is the ONE bibliography entry with neither a comparator-table row nor any relevance sentence in related_work; I verified that by checking all twelve entries. Give it an explicit relevance sentence stating what it actually studies (exponentially tilted INCREMENTAL effects for continuous exposures, their efficiency bound and tilt-dependent minimax lower bounds) and why that is a DIFFERENT target from ours: a tilt/incremental functional rather than the fixed-dose partial mean at an interior point t_0. Do not overstate it as a competitor and do not dismiss it.

TASK 2 — ADD THE POST-STATEMENT DELIMITATION ON thm:oracle-high-s. Immediately after that theorem, delimit it from the two nearest minimax results:
  (a) the incremental/edge continuous-exposure minimax target above — different estimand, so neither theorem implies the other; and
  (b) the closest CATE-minimax fuzzy-hypothesis result, KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE, which gives matching Holder-model minimax rates for BINARY-treatment CATE. State concretely why it does not cover this theorem: binary treatment with no continuous treatment-density smoothness index beta, a conditional-average target rather than a fixed-dose interior partial mean, and therefore no nested beta-class comparison.
  This delimitation is now MORE important than it was, because the note itself carries a fuzzy-hypothesis lower bound (lem:extreme-low-s-fuzzy-lower). Say plainly how ours differs: it is a continuous-dose construction over the present class, giving the exponent r_f = 8/[4 + 2/(alpha v beta) + d/s] that strictly improves the oracle floor when d/s > 4 + 4/alpha - 2/(alpha v beta). Do NOT claim priority over the fuzzy-hypothesis METHOD, which is standard; the novelty is the construction and the exponent for this target and class, not the technique.

TASK 3 — THE WHOLESALE SWEEP, so this class of finding stops recurring. Audit ALL TWELVE bibliography entries in one pass and enforce a single rule: every entry must EITHER carry a theorem-level row in the comparator promise table (naming a specific theorem and the exact difference in target, assumptions and conclusion) OR have an explicit relevance sentence in related_work saying what it is and why it is background rather than a comparator. The twelve are: BonviniKennedy2022FastDRF, KennedyMaMcHughSmall2017, ColangeloLee2025ContinuousDML, RobinsLiTchetgenVanderVaart2008HOIF, LiuMukherjeeRobins2021AdaptiveFunctionals, KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE, BalakrishnanKennedyWasserman2023, SchindlShenKennedy2024Incremental, LimLuedtke2025DataFusion, KimWang2026TwoStageKRR, Tsybakov2009, TakatsuWestling2025DebiasedRegression. Report the disposition of each. Do NOT pad the promise table with rows you cannot substantiate at theorem level — a background sentence is the correct answer for most of these, and an unsubstantiated row is worse than none. Equally, do NOT delete a bibliography entry to make this audit easier.

GUARD: keep every existing correct positioning intact — the incomparability of the accepted prior class (neither lower bound implies the other, the slack condition does not transfer), the attribution of the all-beta oracle-floor RATE SHAPE as prior art, the distinctness of lem:extreme-low-s-fuzzy-lower as a new low-s converse, and the degenerate-boundary framing of the c=1 result. Do not let this round's additions dilute or contradict any of them.

The proof currently displays ONLY the first product. The second, the centering product carrying fbar - f(a), is genuinely missing and must be written down and bounded. The required bound is ADDITIVE in three contributions:
